title: Vanishing of an ideal-power product is detected by affine-cover annihilators
statement: Let X be a scheme, F a quasi-coherent O_X-module, K a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf encoded by IdealSheafData, S a set of affine opens covering every point of X, and t a natural number. With ideal powers and their products as in [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk], K^t F is zero if and only if, for every U in S, K(U)^t is contained in the annihilator of the O_X(U)-module F(U). The convention is K^0=O_X. No finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 01Y9, proof: reduction to an affine covering; affine comparison from Schemes 01I8 and 01IC. The detailed zero-detection argument is the parent node steps 3 and 4.

proof.text: Write J and its inclusion iota for the recursive ideal power and phi for iota tensor F followed by the left unitor. For positive t, the ideal-times theorem gives quasi-coherence of J and range(iota(U)) = K(U)^t. For t=0 these assertions follow from the quasi-coherent structure sheaf and the identity inclusion. The tensor comparison gives quasi-coherence of J tensor F, and the image theorem gives quasi-coherence of the abelian image and equality of its inclusion range with range(phi(U)) on affine opens.

On pure tensors, naturality of tensor sections and the left-unitor formula give phi(U)(a tensor s) = iota(U)(a) times s. If the categorical image is zero, its inclusion is zero, hence phi is zero by its image factorization. Lift any member of K(U)^t through the range formula and evaluate phi on its pure tensor with any section. This proves the annihilator containment on every covering affine.

Conversely, the annihilator hypothesis makes phi zero on every pure tensor of sections over a covering affine. Surjectivity of the tensor-sections comparison and tensor-product induction give phi(U)=0 on all sections. By the affine image formula and injectivity of the image inclusion on sections, sections of the abelian image over each covering affine are subsingleton.

For any quasi-coherent module H with zero sections on an affine U, restrict along its canonical fromSpec chart. The restriction is quasi-coherent, its global sections are zero via restrictAppIso, and the tilde/global-sections counit identifies it with tilde of the zero module; the left adjoint tilde preserves zero. Evaluation and restrictAppIso then give zero sections on every open contained in U, so H restricted to U is zero. The covering hypothesis implies the supremum of the covering opens is top. Apply the existing isZero_of_iSup_eq_top gluing theorem to the abelian image, and transfer zero to the categorical image using Abelian.imageIsoImage. The empty cover requires no separate assumption and t=0 was handled explicitly.

proof_origin.place: Affine reduction in the proof of Stacks 01Y9, with tensor comparison 01I8 and affine equivalence 01IC; implemented through multiplication on pure tensors, affine image sections, and tilde/counit zero detection.

lean.statement:
theorem idealPowerProduct_isZero_iff_affine_cover (X : Scheme.{u})
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (K : X.IdealSheafData)
    (S : Set X.affineOpens) (hS : ∀ x : X, ∃ U ∈ S, x ∈ U.1) (t : ℕ) :
    IsZero (idealModuleProduct (idealSheafPower K.toModulesι t).2 F) ↔
      ∀ U ∈ S, K.ideal U ^ t ≤ Module.annihilator Γ(X, U.1) Γ(F, U.1)
